portfolios._ai_doge_corpus_savings_opportunities: AI-DOGE peer-method ASC levers for a county of this scale: homecare re-procurement and rate benchmarking, technology-enabled care, reablement expansion, and direct-payments growth (method-derived estimates, not the council's own booked plan). NHS Continuing Healthcare is NOT a recovery or saving lever here. NHS England CHC-FNC data (2025/26 Q4) puts NHS Kent and Medway ICB at 54.5 CHC-eligible per 50,000 population aged 18+, rank 10 of 42 ICBs and above the England median of 45.5, so Kent's CHC funding share is a cost-shift exposure to DEFEND if the ICB tightens eligibility, never an under-claiming gap to recover (see directorate_analysis.json asc_chc_position). Kent and Medway is a single ICB footprint that also covers Medway unitary, with no Medway-separable sub-ICB, so Kent-CC-only exposure sizing needs a district-level package base.
